newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler recalls more than 1.74 million vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler recalls more than 1.74 million vehicles.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Monday it is recalling more than 1.74 million cars and trucks for a variety of problems, including air bags that could deploy with the engine turned off and a potential truck fire hazard.

The largest recall involves about 960,000 1994-97 Dodge Ram pickup trucks and 1995-96 Dodge Ram vans and wagons to replace faulty transmission fluid cooling line connectors that have led to 50 reported fires.

Under severe operating conditions, the connectors could melt, allowing transmission fluid to be sprayed onto the truck's exhaust manifold. Chrysler said its dealers will replace the connectors in the repair, which involves all of the Dodge Ram pickups the company has built.
The air bag problem affects about 125,000 1997 model Jeep Wrangler and Cherokee sport utility vehicles, Dodge Dakota pickup trucks and Dodge and Plymouth Neon and Dodge Viper cars, Chrysler said.

The company has received seven reports of air bags inflating spontaneously, about three seconds after the vehicle's ignition being turned off, resulting in two minor injuries. Chrysler said the problem is due to faulty circuitry in the vehicles' air bag control systems, which will be replaced by dealers with redesigned modules.
Chrysler said it will replace the module with one that has redesigned circuits.

The recalls were first disclosed by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in its monthly recall report. Chrysler spokesman Michael McKesson said the actions all had previously been the subject of NHTSA investigations.

He said the large number of vehicles being recalled by Chrysler was a coincidence and did not reflect any changes in the company's recall policies. The automaker has been working hard in recent years to improve its reputation for quality.
"I think if you watch recalls, there's no rhyme or reason as to when they occur," he said. "This is a string that occurred close together."
In the other actions, Chrysler is recalling:

-- 436,000 1992-model Dodge and Plymouth minivans to correct a problem that could cause the rear liftgate's struts to fail, allowing the door to fall suddenly. Chrysler dealers will inspect vans for loose bolts and replace the bolts or struts.

-- 70,000 1992-93 Dodge/Plymouth Colt and Eagle Summit cars to correct seat belt problems that could prevent occupants from being properly restrained in a crash. The Colt and Summit cars were made by Mitsubishi Motors Corp. in Japan.
-- 148,000 Dodge Shadow and Plymouth Sundance cars to replace a bolt that attaches the lower seat back to the seat bottom, which could separate and increase the risk of a crash.

-- 1,083 Eagle Talon, Dodge Avenger and Chrysler Sebring cars to replace the seat back assembly due to a faulty head restraint support bracket that could break, increasing the risk of personal injury. Mitsubishi, which supplies the cars to Chrysler, is taking similar action on 119 Eclipse models.

In other actions, NHTSA said it has opened a safety investigation into Ford Motor Co.'s F-150 pickup trucks for the possibility that the vehicle could roll away after the transmission is shifted into the "park" position. Three consumers described such incidents, resulting in one crash.

NHTSA also said it upgraded a probe into 291,998 1991-94 Ford Explorer sport utility vehicles because of reports that glass sunroofs shattered or separated from the vehicle while driving. NHTSA said the investigation was in the testing stage.
